newsitem.title: INDIA: India accepts wanted bandit's terms for surrender.
newsitem.headline: India accepts wanted bandit's terms for surrender.

text.p: The government of a southern Indian state has accepted India's most wanted bandit's terms for surrender, which include top commando protection, senior officials said on Monday.
"We have agreed to the surrender proposal and to protect Veerappan's life," Karnataka state Law Minister M.C. Nanaiah told reporters in the state capital, Bangalore.
In 1994 Veerappan set terms for his surrender at a hefty bribe, a general amnesty and top commando protection for himself as well as jobs for his men.
Paramilitary officials then said the terms for the dreaded sandalwood smuggler and elephant poacher's surrender were impossible.
"We have not agreed to the amnesty," a senior police official told Reuters on Monday.

The elusive gang leader is currently holding nine forest department officials hostage. He has been operating for more than two decades from a thick sandalwood forest straddling the southern states of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
"It is not a question of victory or defeat. It is an inevitable decision that has to be taken in the present context," Nanaiah told reporters.
It was not immediately clear whether the government had accepted Veerappan's demand for 10 billion rupees ($280 million) as part of the deal.
Police say he is wanted for at least 60 murders, mostly of policemen, and for the poaching of at least 500 elephants and smuggling sandalwood, an officially controlled commodity. ($1=35.7 rupees)
